name: Zetam
title: Levites in Temple Service
summary: Zetam was a Levite, the son of Ladan (also known as Libni), from the clan of the Gershonites. He served in connection with the temple treasury and the management of the treasures of the house of the Lord during King David's reign. He is mentioned in the genealogies in 1 Chronicles as part of the Levitical service arrangement.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Genealogy of the Gershonites
keyEvents.description: Zetam is listed as a son of Ladan in the genealogical line of the Gershonites among the Levites, who were organized for service in the temple.

keyEvents.title: Service over the Treasures of the House of the Lord
keyEvents.description: Zetam and his brothers were responsible for managing the treasures in the house of the Lord, an important role in the temple administration during David's rule.

keyEvents.title: David's Organization of the Levites
keyEvents.description: As part of David's extensive organization of the Levitical service, Zetam was assigned a specific role in the management of the sanctuary.

keyEvents.title: The heads of the Gershonite families
keyEvents.description: Zethan was counted among the heads of the families of the Gershonites, who were one of the three main branches of the tribe of Levi.
